title: Letter 23 — Against Despairing Thoughts
attribution_note: Letter 23 of 46 in the collection Letters Sent — see Letter 1 for provenance.

sections.heading: I also have felt the same

pairs.en: I hear that thoughts trouble thee and cast thee into despair; wherefore I offer thee, according to my strength, my counsel for thy comfort.

1) I myself have felt the same in myself, and now often feel it, whence cometh fear, and horror, and anguish; and I mark the same in others also, for it befalleth not thee alone. Yet of salvation in Christ I despair not, and I *“look for the resurrection of the dead, and the life of the world to come,”* as we read in the Creed — which I counsel both to others and to thee.

2) Mark what Holy Scripture saith for our comfort, to us who are sinners and troubled: *“This is a faithful saying, and worthy of all acceptation, that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners; of whom I am chief,”* saith the apostle Paul [1 Timothy 1:15]. Therefore He will save us also, sinners, seeing that we also are sinners. And again: *“the Son of man”* (that is, Christ) *“is come to seek and to save that which was lost”* [Luke 19:10].

Therefore He will seek us also, seeing that we also are of them that were lost. And again: *“I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance,”* saith Christ [Matthew 9:13]. And again: *“For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.* *For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved,”* saith Christ [John 3:16–17].

From this one may conclude that Christ came into the world not to judge us, but to save; and He will save us without fail, if we truly believe in Him. He shall come the second time to judge. But whom? Not simply sinners, but sinners unrepentant; but to repentant sinners who believe in Him, to declare the mercy and blessing of His heavenly Father, and to bring them into His heavenly kingdom; to them He saith: *“Come, ye blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world”* [Matthew 25:34].

Therefore there is hope for repenting sinners; there is comfort for them that mourn and are sorrowful. The doors of the mercy of God *“are opened”* unto them that knock; their petition *“is given”* unto them that ask; God with all the heavenly treasure *“is found”* of them that seek [Matthew 7:7–8]. Thieves, publicans, fornicators and other repenting sinners enter into everlasting life. There is hope for us sinners also, seeing that God *“regardeth not persons”* [Deuteronomy 10:17], but hath mercy upon all repenting sinners alike, and saveth them.

sections.heading: With the thief upon the cross

pairs.en: 3) When such a thought cometh upon us: how shall we be with the apostles, the prophets, the martyrs and the other great saints, who have shone in so many virtues? — let us answer our thought thus: we desire to be with the thief, who at the very end of his life uttered one cry with repentance: *“Lord, remember me when thou comest into thy kingdom”* — and heard from Christ hanging upon the Cross: *“Verily I say unto thee, To day shalt thou be with me in paradise”* [Luke 23:42–43]. And if we be with that thief in paradise, then also with Christ Himself, seeing that that thief is with Christ in paradise, and therefore also with all the saints. For where Christ is, there are all the saints also. Let us pray, then, unto Christ with the thief: *“Lord, remember me when thou comest into thy kingdom.”* And again: *“I believe, O Lord, and I confess that Thou art truly the Christ, the Son of the living God, who camest into the world to save sinners, of whom I am chief: I pray Thee therefore, have mercy upon me,”* and the rest.

4) Troubling thoughts that draw into despair come from the devil, who would cast us into utter despair and so destroy us; because despair is a heavy sin, for he who despaireth of his salvation thinketh that God is not merciful and not true — and this is a fearful blasphemy against God. Unto such a heavy sin doth Satan desire to bring us through troubling and despairing thoughts. This his fierce temptation must we resist, and establish ourselves in hope upon the mercy of God, and look for our salvation from Him. When such thoughts come upon thee, pray thus: *“Forsake me not, O LORD: O my God, be not far from me.* *Make haste to help me, O Lord my salvation”* [Psalm 38:21–22]! And again: *“LORD, how are they increased that trouble me! many are they that rise up against me.* *Many there be which say of my soul, There is no help for him in God.* *But thou, O LORD, art a shield for me,”* and so on to the end of the third psalm.

sections.heading: These thoughts, though heavy, are profitable

pairs.en: 5) Though these thoughts are grievous unto us, yet are they profitable, seeing that through them we are drawn away from the vanity of the world. And so that which Satan, by the permission of God, worketh for our evil, God by His mercy turneth unto our good, if we ourselves faint not, but strive against them.

6) Whoso feeleth such thoughts and fighteth against them — this is a sign that such a one is in the faith and in grace. For Satan fighteth not against him who obeyeth him and serveth him, but fighteth only against them that resist him, and would by those thoughts cast them down. Therefore men who love the vanity of this world — honour, glory, riches, luxury — feel not such wounding thoughts. And thou, if thou lovedst this vanity, wouldest not feel them. But because Satan marketh that thou hast turned from vanity and seekest salvation, he fighteth against thee with these thoughts, and would bring thee into despair and so destroy thee. Take heed, then, of this craft of the enemy. Mark also them that love vanity, and them that have turned from it and seek God, and thou shalt know that I write the truth. Truly, all they that seek salvation complain of these thoughts; and on the contrary, they feel them not who are comforted with the delights of this world.

Let Satan devise his evil against us; but we must do our own work — that is, to strive against sin, to establish ourselves in faith and hope, to endeavour to do what is pleasing unto God, to subject our will to the will of God, often to pray unto God and ask help of Him against the devil and against sin, and in this struggle not to faint, and so to be established in the hope of salvation. He can do nothing unto us, for Christ is our Helper and Saviour — Christ, who hath cast him down. Upon Him let us cast our trust — and we shall not be ashamed. With the Psalmist let us boldly sing the song: *“The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear?”* (and so on, the twenty-seventh psalm).

7) Woe unto sinners unrepentant, because the judgment of God awaiteth them. But they that repent and seek their salvation by prayer and faith must look for the mercy of God: *“for with the LORD there is mercy, and with him is plenteous redemption.* *And he shall redeem Israel from all his iniquities”* [Psalm 130:7–8]. *“Thy mercy, O LORD, endureth for ever: forsake not the works of thine own hands”* [Psalm 138:8]. *“Our soul waiteth for the LORD: he is our help and our shield.* *For our heart shall rejoice in him, because we have trusted in his holy name.* *Let thy mercy, O LORD, be upon us, according as we hope in thee”* [Psalm 33:20–22].
Read this through, and consider, and be strengthened. The Lord help thee. And remember me also, a sinner.
